title: Research on the Pathway of AI Technology Empowering the Development of Core Competencies in Middle School Mathematics
venue: Journal of Educational Theory and Practice
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how AI technology can support the development of core mathematical competencies in middle school mathematics, especially under conditions where traditional class-based instruction struggles to provide personalized guidance, timely feedback, and visualization of abstract thinking. The author frames the problem as a mismatch between broad, uniform teaching and the precise, differentiated cultivation of competencies such as abstraction, reasoning, modeling, intuitive imagination, operation, and data analysis.

Rather than reporting an empirical intervention, the paper proposes a conceptual pathway for AI-enabled mathematics teaching. It describes five functional roles of AI in education—intelligent diagnosis, personalized recommendation, interactive feedback, visualization of thinking, and automated processing—and maps them onto the six middle-school mathematics competency dimensions. Examples include using VR/AR to support abstraction, dynamic geometry and 3D modeling to strengthen intuition and imagination, stepwise reasoning support and error diagnosis to improve logical reasoning and calculation, and data visualization and scenario simulation to support modeling and data analysis.

The paper focuses on middle school mathematics in the Chinese education context and argues that AI can make instruction more personalized, visual, and precise. It also identifies implementation challenges such as over-instrumentalization, limited teacher AI competence, uneven resource quality, and student foundation constraints. The conclusion recommends competency-oriented design, teacher training, student AI literacy development, and higher-quality resource construction, but it does not present outcome data from a specific classroom study.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/theoretical paper rather than an empirical evaluation. It does not report a research design, sample, comparison condition, or outcome data, so it provides no basis for causal or correlational evidence grading beyond grey-literature style analysis.
impact_tier_rationale: No empirical impacts are reported. The paper discusses potential instructional pathways and implementation challenges, but it does not measure learning gains, engagement, or efficiency effects.

interventions.use_case: Conceptual use of ChatGPT-like generative AI as an intelligent interaction tool to support middle school mathematics learning through question answering, prompt-based guidance, personalized feedback, and thinking scaffolds for abstraction, reasoning, modeling, visualization, and data analysis.
